lq.q: Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=x^3\) in \((-\pi,\pi)\). Using Parseval's identity, prove that \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^6}=\frac{\pi^6}{945}\).
answer: Step Marks Since \(x^3\) is odd, \(a_0=0\), \(a_n=0\) (2) \(b_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}x^3\sin nx\,dx=\frac{2(-1)^{n+1}}{n}\left(\pi^2-\frac{6}{n^2}\right)\) (5) Thus, \(x^3=2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{n+1}\left(\frac{\pi^2}{n}-\frac{6}{n^3}\right)\sin nx\) (3) Parseval's: \(\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}x^6 dx=\frac{1}{2}\sum b_n^2\) ⇒ \(\frac{2\pi^6}{7}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left[\frac{4\pi^4}{n^2}-\frac{48\pi^2}{n^4}+\frac{144}{n^6}\right]\) (4) Using known sums, solve for \(\sum\frac{1}{n^6}\) (1)
